label: D2 after choosing a1, in the last ~10 trials of the episode
explanation: Fires almost exclusively at D2 (100% of mass) when the GO choice just made was a1 (99.6% of mass; the action input at D2 is observed), and only in the final trials of the 100-trial episode: zero activations before trial 80, 98% of mass in trials 90-99. Equivalently it tracks the model value being low (value < 5.22 holds 98% of mass), since value falls as the episode end nears. It is stronger when the reached state is S1 (83% of mass), but S2 after a1 also fires, more so very late. Silent at D1 and GO, after a2, and early in the episode. Dev: ep_trial>=90 gives mass recall 0.97 (P 0.68); >=92 gives F1 0.81 (P 0.79, R 0.83). Coverage of the higher activation quartiles is near complete, while the weakest quartile is where misses (trials 88-91, rare a2 cases) fall. All variables used are observable (the agent must keep an internal clock).

issues: All the factual claims check out on dev. D2 holds 100% of the activation mass: 11205 of 11219 active steps, with 14 tiny D1 hits and 0 at GO. in_action==1 holds 99.6% of the mass. There are no activations before trial 80, and trials 90-99 hold 97.7%. value<5.22 holds 97.8%. in_state==1 holds 82.8%. The predicate scores dev P 0.793 / R 0.835 / F1 0.814 / mass recall 0.919, consistent with the reported test numbers (0.815 / 0.819 / 0.817 / 0.913).

The ep_trial cutoff sits on a smooth ramp, not a sharp edge. Given D2 & a1, the firing rate climbs steadily with ep_trial: t=88 0.07, t=90 0.25, t=91 0.35, t=92 0.50, t=93 0.63, t=94 0.78, t=95 0.88, then t=96-99 0.92-0.97. Both the false positives near 92-93 and the misses at 88-91 come from this graded ramp, not from a separate counterexample class. The label's 'last ~10 trials' is slightly loose: activity is reliable only in roughly the last 6-8 trials.

On test, the false positives are mostly at trials 92-94. A disproportionate share are a1 trials that land in S2 or have good=S2, but precision stays about the same across subgroups (good, prev_action, prev_reward, start_high, in_state 0.68-0.84). The S1 effect is a modulation, not a gate: ep_trial>=92 & in_state==2 gives P 0.676, versus 0.836 for in_state==1.

Misses on test are scattered weak activations, mostly at trial 89-91 and some a2 D2 steps, at about 0.05-0.3 of max. They hold 8.7% of the mass. No systematic phase, choice, transition or reward pattern turned up.

Small improvement: requiring low value as well near the boundary, (phase==D2)&(in_action==1)&(ep_trial>=90)&(value<5.2), gives test F1 0.826 vs 0.817. That is marginal and agrees with the explanation's own reading (value falls as the episode end approaches). No future variables are involved.
